_meta: A nested list (a 2x2 matrix), used to show the shallow-vs-deep copy trap: copying a nested structure with a slice, list(), or .copy() makes a SHALLOW copy -- a new outer list whose elements are the SAME inner objects as the original -- so mutating an inner element through the copy also mutates the original. matrix is the fixture: a list of rows, each row itself a list. A shallow copy (matrix[:], list(matrix), matrix.copy()) duplicates only the top level: the new list is a distinct object (appending a whole new row to it does not affect the original), but its elements point at the very same row lists as the original, so copy[0] IS original[0]. Appending to copy[0] therefore appends to original[0] too -- the mutation leaks. A DEEP copy (copy.deepcopy) recursively duplicates every level, so the copy's rows are independent new lists and mutating them leaves the original untouched. The trap is that shallow copying LOOKS like it made an independent copy (the outer list is independent) and only fails when you reach into the nested level, which is exactly what most code does. matrix is the fixture; the shallow and deep copies, their inner-object identities, and the effect of mutating each on the original are computed.
